content.title: Replacing Wordy Phrasing for Concision
content.overview: The ACT English section rewards brevity and directness. This lesson focuses on identifying 'wordy signal phrases'—multi-word expressions that function as a single part of speech—and replacing them with concise, one-word or two-word alternatives to improve sentence flow without changing the meaning.
learning_objectives: Identify common wordy signal phrases that clutter sentences.
Select the most concise replacement that maintains the original grammatical structure.
Apply the Signal-Rewrite-Check strategy to eliminate unnecessary words.
Distinguish between concise replacements and wordy distractors.

sections.title: Identifying Wordy Signal Phrases
sections.content: Wordy signal phrases are groups of words that can be replaced by a single word without losing any information. These often appear as 'filler' around logical transitions. Common examples include 'because of the fact that' (replace with 'because'), 'in the event that' (replace with 'if'), and 'at this point in time' (replace with 'now'). On the ACT, if a shorter option provides the same meaning and is grammatically correct, it is almost always the right answer.

sections.title: The Signal-Rewrite-Check Strategy
sections.content: To handle these questions effectively, follow three steps: 1. Signal: Spot the multi-word expression that feels heavy or repetitive. 2. Rewrite: Swap the phrase for a single concise equivalent (e.g., change 'due to the fact that' to 'because'). 3. Check: Ensure the new word fits the grammar of the sentence. For instance, 'because' must be followed by a subject and a verb, while 'due to' is followed by a noun phrase.

sections.title: Grammar Fit and Syntax
sections.content: When shortening a phrase, you must ensure the surrounding sentence structure still works. If you replace a long prepositional phrase with a conjunction, the words following it must form a clause. If you replace it with a preposition, the words following it must be a noun or noun phrase. A concise answer is only correct if it is also grammatically sound.

worked_examples.question:
The marathon was cancelled [due to the fact that there was] a severe thunderstorm warning in the area. 

A. NO CHANGE 
B. because of the fact that there was 
C. because of 
D. in light of the fact that there was
worked_examples.solution: Step 1 (Signal): The phrase 'due to the fact that there was' is wordy. Step 2 (Rewrite): Look for a shorter way to express cause. 'Because of' is much shorter. Step 3 (Check): 'The marathon was cancelled because of a severe thunderstorm warning.' This is grammatically correct (preposition + noun phrase) and preserves the meaning. Choice C is the most concise.

worked_examples.question:
[In the event that] the store is closed, we will have to drive to the next town. 

A. NO CHANGE 
B. If 
C. In the case that 
D. Should it be that
worked_examples.solution: Step 1 (Signal): 'In the event that' is a four-word phrase signaling a condition. Step 2 (Rewrite): The word 'If' serves the exact same purpose. Step 3 (Check): 'If the store is closed...' is a standard dependent clause. Choice B is the most direct and concise option.

common_mistakes: Choosing a 'formal' sounding phrase: Students often think 'due to the fact that' sounds more academic, but the ACT prefers 'because'.
Ignoring grammar fit: Replacing a phrase with a shorter word that creates a fragment or a run-on.

Redundant replacements: Choosing an option that is shorter than the original but still contains unnecessary words (e.g., replacing 'at this point in time' with 'at this time' when 'now' is an option).
exam_tips: The 'Shortest is Best' Rule: If multiple choices are grammatically correct and mean the same thing, the shortest one is usually the winner.
Watch for 'Fact That': Any phrase containing 'the fact that' is a major red flag for wordiness.
Read the whole sentence: Ensure your concise replacement doesn't accidentally change the tense or the relationship between ideas.
content.recap: Concision is about removing 'dead wood' from sentences. Replace multi-word signals like 'because of the fact that' with direct equivalents like 'because.' Always verify that your shorter choice maintains the original meaning and fits the sentence's grammatical structure.

knowledge_claims.content: A wordy signal phrase is a multi-word expression that can be replaced by a single word or a shorter phrase without changing the sentence's meaning.
The Signal-Rewrite-Check strategy involves identifying a wordy phrase, swapping it for a concise equivalent, and verifying the resulting grammar.
On the ACT English section, if two options are both grammatically correct and mean the same thing, the more concise option is preferred.
The phrase 'because of the fact that' is a wordy version of the conjunction 'because'.
The phrase 'in the event that' is a wordy version of the conditional conjunction 'if'.
The phrase 'at this point in time' is a wordy version of the adverb 'now'.
When replacing a wordy phrase, you must ensure the replacement matches the required part of speech (e.g., using a conjunction to join clauses).
A common mistake is selecting a phrase like 'due to the fact that' because it sounds more formal, even though it is less concise than 'because'.
The inclusion of the words 'the fact that' within a phrase is a common indicator that the phrasing is unnecessarily wordy.
To maintain grammatical fit, 'because' should be followed by a clause (subject + verb), whereas 'because of' should be followed by a noun phrase.
Replacing wordy phrasing does not mean removing essential information; it means expressing the same information in fewer words.
Phrases like 'owing to the fact that' and 'in light of the fact that' are typically distractors for the more concise 'because' or 'since'.

items.stem:
Practice form 1. Rina is editing a short report about a community garden.

Which choice expresses the idea most directly?
A) due to the fact that
B) for the reason that
C) because
D) on account of the fact that

options.D: on account of the fact that

items.explanation: The correct choice directly applies the target skill: 用更简洁直接的表达替换赘述.

videoLesson.title: Replace Wordy Phrases With Concision
videoLesson.description: Recognize wordy signal phrases and concise alternatives in sentences. Swap the flagged wording for one grammatically fitting expression and adjust surrounding grammar to preserve meaning.
